paper.central_claim: AgentFactory preserves successful task solutions as executable Python subagent code (with SKILL.md), refines saved subagents from execution feedback on later similar tasks, and thereby reduces the effort (orchestrator tokens) needed for similar tasks without manual intervention; subagents are portable to other Python-capable agent systems.
paper.title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse

evidence.quote: We propose AgentFactory, a new self-evolution paradigm that preserves successful task solutions as executable subagent code rather than textual experience.
evidence.support_explanation: States the changed non-weight object: stored experience is executable code instead of text.

evidence.quote: Upon successful completion, the Meta-Agent evaluates the subagent and decides which skills to save as reusable skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention/admission decision is made by the same LLM Meta-Agent; no replay, held-out or statistical gate is described.

evidence.quote: The modified subagent is tested against the current task to verify the improvement.
evidence.support_explanation: Validation of a modification is on the triggering task only; no regression check on previously solved tasks is described.

evidence.quote: Upon successful completion, results and improved subagents are promoted from the workspace to the persistent skill library.
evidence.support_explanation: Gives the persistence path: isolated workspace, then promotion to library. No versioning/rollback/retirement is described.

evidence.quote: consists of 15 additional tasks with similar structure but different specific requirements, serving as transfer evaluation targets.
evidence.support_explanation: Batch 2 is built to mirror Batch 1 (Appendix B), so reuse is tested on near-variants authored by the same team.

evidence.quote: We report the average output token count of the orchestrating model per task, excluding token consumption within subagent LLM calls.
evidence.support_explanation: Sole quantitative metric is orchestrator output tokens; subagent LLM cost is excluded, so cost may be shifted rather than saved.

evidence.quote: We ensure that all tasks are completed without runtime errors in all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Task quality is not scored; completion without runtime error is the only success condition mentioned.

evidence.quote: A notable finding is that Opus 4.6 already shows a significant reduction in orchestration tokens during Batch 1 itself under AgentFactory (4324 vs. 8298 for ReAct)
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported Opus result; Batch 1 reduction occurs before any transfer, so it cannot be attributed to retained subagents from other batches.

evidence.quote: AgentFactory Batch 1 (from scratch) 4324 9199 Batch 2 (w/ saved) 2971 3862
evidence.support_explanation: Table values (Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6): AgentFactory Batch 1 Sonnet 9199 exceeds ReAct Batch 1 Sonnet 6893; Batch 2 values 2971/3862 vs ReAct 7022/7029 and textual-experience 6210/8223. Single run per cell, no variance.

evidence.quote: This shows the agent autonomously detecting limitations and improving error handling through iterative refinement.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-evolve step is supported by one qualitative README-subagent example over three runs; no quantification.

evidence.quote: the agent writes and executes code for each task, and saves the resulting experience as textual summaries
evidence.support_explanation: Textual-experience baseline is described in one sentence; retrieval, store size and prompts are not specified.

evidence.quote: However, these approaches primarily record successful experiences as textual prompts, verbal reflections, or reasoning traces.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prior self-evolution stores text; claimed to fail at reliable efficient re-execution (asserted, not measured).

evidence.quote: or by saving executable tool-level skills, as demonstrated by Voyager
evidence.support_explanation: The closest executable-skill-library neighbor is named in one clause; no comparison or differentiation is given in text or experiments.

evidence.quote: In Trajectory 3, the workflow migrated to Claude Code—a different agent system—which first learned how to use the saved subagents by reading the SKILL.md documentation.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-system portability is one anecdote with no metric.

evidence.quote: We consistently use the same LLM backbone for both the MetaAgent and subagents across all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Same backbone for all arms; two backbones tested (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6).

evidence.quote: Token counts exclude subagent-internal LLM consumption.
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the cost metric omits the delegated work and creation/modification calls.

evidence.quote: We ensure that all tasks are completed without runtime errors in all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: 'Ensure' implies runs were checked and, where needed, redone until error-free. The number of failed/rerun attempts and their tokens are not reported, so the per-task means exclude a failure denominator. Also, 'no runtime error' is the only correctness criterion.

evidence.quote: A notable finding is that Opus 4.6 already shows a significant reduction in orchestration tokens during Batch 1 itself under AgentFactory (4324 vs. 8298 for ReAct)
evidence.support_explanation: Before any cross-batch reuse, the delegating architecture already halves the counted tokens, because subagent-internal calls are excluded from the count. The Batch 2 contrast with ReAct therefore mixes reuse with an accounting/architecture effect.

evidence.quote: running the second batch with subagents created when evaluating on the first batch
evidence.support_explanation: AgentFactory has only two rows (Batch 1 from scratch, Batch 2 with saved). There is no AgentFactory-on-Batch-2-from-scratch row, i.e. no same-scaffold store-off on the evaluated tasks.

gap.author_gap: Self-evolving agents store experience as text, which cannot reliably guarantee efficient re-execution in complex scenarios.
gap.checked_gap: A real design axis (text vs executable store), but the claim that text fails is asserted and only indirectly tested via an under-specified textual baseline; no dedicated test of executable vs text reliability.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion/Self-Refine (text reflection), Voyager (executable skill library; named only), AlphaEvolve and Darwin Goedel Machine (code evolution for specialized problems). Voyager-style executable skill accumulation is the closest neighbor and is neither differentiated nor compared against.
gap.residue: No evidence yet on correctness of reused subagents, admission quality, or library degradation over many tasks.
gap.stakes: Re-derivation cost on recurring procedural tasks.
gap.method_response: Store solutions as code with docs and refine on failure; deploy to other agent frameworks.
gap.remaining_gap: Quality-controlled admission, regression-safe modification, true held-out transfer, and total cost accounting remain open.
unresolved: Whether code store beats a well-built text/skill store on correctness (not only orchestrator tokens)

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 15 authored near-variant tasks, an LLM orchestrator that reuses its own saved Python subagents emits fewer orchestrator output tokens than ReAct and a textual-memory agent; subagent-internal cost and output correctness are not measured.
unresolved: Opus: no AgentFactory Batch-2-from-scratch row (same-scaffold store-off) (opus:O03).
Opus: failed/rerun attempts behind 'we ensure … without runtime errors' are not counted (opus:O01).
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; nothing was run by us. Central claim 'increasingly robust and efficient as more tasks are encountered' is retained as stated; supported conclusion is narrower.
assessment.evidence_level_note: A self-written library is retained and read on separate Batch 2 tasks, but the improvement is never isolated from the architecture: there is no same-scaffold store-off, Batch 1 already shows the token drop without reuse, and the count excludes subagent calls. EVIDENCE 'retained' requires the retained change to produce the gain; here that is not shown. Contrast SWE-Exp (r-precedent), which had a same-scaffold k=0 control.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The text-vs-executable-store axis is real, but 'text cannot guarantee re-execution' is asserted, and the closest neighbour (Voyager's executable skill library) is named only, never differentiated.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. Create → save-on-success (Meta-Agent judgement) → retrieve → modify-on-failure → validate on the current task is a coherent chain, but it is the Voyager-style recipe. The paper offers no reasoned prediction that separates it from a code-skill library or from a well-built text store. Admission rests on an LLM's judgement of 'successful completion'. sol's 3 credits plausibility that anchor 2 already covers.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Create/modify/save/list/view primitives, workspace isolation and promotion are reconstructible. Validation is on the current task only, with no regression replay, versioning, rollback or retirement.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The only metric is orchestrator output tokens, excluding subagent-internal LLM calls. 'Success' means no runtime error, and chart/report/booking correctness is never checked (opus:O01).

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. Same-backbone ReAct and textual-experience baselines exist, but the key alternative explanation is untested: the delegation architecture moves work into uncounted subagent calls. Opus Batch 1 already shows 4324 vs 8298 before any reuse (opus:O02), and there is no same-scaffold store-off on Batch 2 (opus:O03). Nothing ablates save/modify/tool allocation, and Sonnet Batch 1 (9199 > 6893) contradicts the within-batch claim. Budget non-parity is charged here and in E.cost (A2).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The library is built on Batch 1 and read on 15 separate Batch 2 tasks. Those tasks are 1:1 mirrored variants (the H07 'fixed input shape' failure), it is not stated whether the library is frozen during Batch 2, and the cross-system claim is a single anecdote.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): n=15 per cell, and a negative cell (Sonnet Batch 1) is visible. Single runs, no variance; reruns behind 'we ensure' are uncounted (opus:O01).

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1. Cost is the headline, but it counts only orchestrator output tokens. Subagent calls, input tokens, latency and the cost of building/modifying subagents are absent.

reason: Complete pinned v1 HTML text (with Appendices A–B) read. In scope (system_method): executable subagent code is written from execution feedback, retained, and read on later tasks. All eight items resolved.

resolutions.reason: See assessment.evidence_level_note. Without a same-scaffold store-off, and with Batch 1 already showing the effect, the retained library is not shown to produce the gain. sol's 'retained' treats 'the change was kept and reused' as 'the kept change improved later tasks'.

H07 already covers the traceback-driven repair of a forged tool ('debug it against execution feedback, and register it'). son55's H12 (low fit) needs recurring-mechanism diagnosis over harness code plus a replay/regression promotion gate, and neither is present. The modify step is H07's repair loop on reuse, not a second pattern.
Same question in both seats (total efficiency including delegated calls). sol's 'partial' rests on the very exclusion that makes it unmet: subagent calls are excluded by design.
Verified: modified subagents are validated only on the current task, with no regression check on earlier tasks and no rollback.
Verified: the added structure's own cost (subagent LLM calls, creation, modification) is the part excluded from the only cost metric.
Verified: there is no ablation of save, modify or tool allocation, and no same-scaffold store-off (opus:O03).
Verified: Batch 1 spans several domains, but Batch 2 mirrors it 1:1, and cross-system use is one anecdote.
Verified: ReAct and a textual-experience agent are compared; no executable-library neighbour (Voyager) is.
Verified: the bottleneck is asserted. The textual-experience comparison probes it only indirectly, through a confounded token metric.
Failure mode partly present (son55 convention: met = avoided). The forged subagent is measured only through whole-framework orchestrator tokens, never as an isolated artefact.
See ratings.M: coherent chain, but no prediction distinguishes it from the named Voyager-style library.

See ratings.E.causality: the architecture/accounting alternative (opus:O02) and the missing same-scaffold store-off (opus:O03) leave the reuse effect unisolated. sol's 2 treats the ReAct and text baselines as isolating the narrow efficiency gap.
